parts.watchFor: Watch how Ibrahim thinks his way to God, and how he speaks to his angry father.

questions.q: Why could Ibrahim not bow to the idols?
options: They were made by human hands

questions.q: What did Ibrahim say when the star set?
options: I do not love things that set

questions.q: How did Ibrahim speak to his father about the idols?
options: Gently, asking why he worshipped what could not hear or see

lesson.text: Ibrahim used his mind: anything that rises and sets cannot be God. Then he spoke gently, even to a father who drove him away. Seek the truth with your mind, and share it with kindness.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour Ibrahim, known in the Bible as Abraham, for reasoning his way to one God, and for speaking gently even to his angry father.

carry.title: Ibrahim's turning to God, said at the start of prayer

reflect.muslim: Who in your family do you disagree with about faith? How could you speak to them as gently as Ibrahim did?
reflect.curious: Have you ever changed your mind by thinking something through? What helped?

parts.act: Speak gently to someone in your family you disagree with.

parts.watchFor: Ibrahim breaks the idols and is thrown into a fire. Watch what the fire does.

questions.q: Which idol did Ibrahim leave unbroken?
What did the fire do to Ibrahim?
options: It went out before he reached it

questions.q: What did Ibrahim tell the king who claimed to give life and death?
options: My Lord brings the sun up from the east; bring it up from the west

lesson.text: Ibrahim stood for the truth alone against a whole city, and God told the fire to be cool and safe for him. Speak for what is true, and trust that God is in control.
lesson.curious: In the Quran's telling, God made the fire cool and safe for Ibrahim. Muslims see in it courage for the truth, and trust in God when everything seems against you.

reflect.muslim: Where do you need courage to stand for what's right right now?
reflect.curious: When have you had to stand alone for something you believed? What did it cost?

parts.act: When you feel afraid this week, say: God is enough for me, and He is the best to rely on.

parts.watchFor: Hajar is left in a barren valley with her baby. Watch what she says, and what she does.

questions.q: What did Hajar ask Ibrahim as he turned to go?
How many times did Hajar run between Safa and Marwa?
What welled up from the ground where Ismail lay?

lesson.text: Hajar trusted God completely: then He will not abandon us. And still she ran, seven times, looking for help. Trust and effort go together, and God answered her with the spring of Zamzam.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour Hajar, known in the Bible as Hagar, for her trust in God and her tireless effort. Pilgrims still walk between Safa and Marwa as she ran.

carry.title: Ibrahim's prayer to keep up the prayer

reflect.muslim: What are you worried about right now? What would Hajar's trust, and Hajar's running, look like for it?
reflect.curious: When things look hopeless, do you tend to wait or to act? What does Hajar's story suggest?

parts.act: Do your part fully on something you're anxious about, then leave the outcome to God.

parts.watchFor: Ibrahim sees a dream about his son. Watch how both father and son answer God's command.

questions.q: What did Ibrahim do after his dream?
options: Told Ismail and asked what he thought

questions.q: What did Ibrahim drive Satan off with on the way?
What stood in the boy's place?

lesson.text: Ibrahim and Ismail were both ready to give God what they loved most, and God ransomed Ismail with a great ram. What God wanted was their surrender, and they gave it. Muslims remember this every Eid al-Adha.
lesson.curious: Muslims remember this story every year at Eid al-Adha: Ibrahim's readiness to obey, Ismail's willingness, and God's mercy in ransoming him.

carry.title: Ibrahim's prayer for a righteous child

reflect.muslim: What do you love so much that it would be hard to give up for God? Ask Him to keep it in its right place in your heart.
reflect.curious: What would you find hardest to give up for something you believed in?

parts.act: Give up one thing you love this week for God's sake, even something small.

parts.watchFor: Three guests arrive at Ibrahim's tent. Watch how he welcomes them, and what he builds.

questions.q: What did Ibrahim bring his guests?
What did Ismail do while his father built the House?
What is the stone Ibrahim stood on called?

lesson.text: Ibrahim welcomed guests generously, pleaded gently even for people facing punishment, and built God's House with his son, praying that God would accept it. God took him as a close friend.
lesson.curious: Muslims call Ibrahim the Friend of God. They remember his generosity to guests and the House he built with Ismail, the Kaaba in Makkah.

carry.title: Ibrahim and Ismail's prayer as they built

reflect.muslim: When you finish something good, do you ask God to accept it, as Ibrahim did?
reflect.curious: Who do you know that is generous the way Ibrahim was with his guests? What makes them that way?

parts.act: Welcome a guest or a newcomer this week the way Ibrahim did: quickly and generously.
